cases.path: Fix is confirmed and released, so the issue is closed as completed
cases.title: [AVM Module Issue]: Allow overriding the AzAPI resource type and API version
cases.body:
### Description

The module pins the AzAPI API versions it uses internally. When a newer API version exposes a property we need, we have to wait for a module release rather than opting in ourselves.

### Proposed

Expose the `<provider>/<resource>@<api-version>` strings as an input so a caller can override them, keeping the current values as defaults:

```hcl
module "example" {
  source = "Azure/avm-ptn-example-repo/azurerm"

  resource_types = {
    network_virtual_networks = "Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks@2025-05-01"
  }
}
```

### Module version

`v0.1.1`

<!-- regr:fix-released -->

cases.title: [AVM Module Issue]: Use the shared interfaces utility module instead of inline definitions
cases.body:
### Description

The module hard-codes its role assignment and lock logic inline instead of consuming the shared AVM interfaces utility module. This means interface changes have to be re-implemented here by hand, and the module drifts from the AVM interface spec between releases.

### Proposed

Consume `Azure/avm-utl-interfaces/azurerm` for the role assignment and lock interfaces so the shapes stay aligned with the spec automatically.

### Module version

`v0.1.2`

<!-- regr:fix-unreleased -->

cases.title: Question: does this module create the resource group or expect an existing one?
cases.body:
### Question

Does this module create the resource group for me, or does it expect one to already exist?

I have a resource group provisioned by a separate pipeline and I want the virtual network placed into it. I can see a `resource_group_name` input but it is not clear from the README whether supplying it means "use this existing group" or "create a group with this name".

A one-line note in the README would settle it.

<!-- avm-triage-regression-fixture -->

cases.title: Bug: diagnostic settings are left behind after terraform destroy
cases.body:
### Describe the bug

Diagnostic settings created by the module are not removed by `terraform destroy`. The virtual network and subnets are destroyed correctly, but the diagnostic setting stays attached to the (now deleted) resource and shows up as an orphan in the portal.

Re-running `terraform apply` afterwards then fails because the diagnostic setting name is already taken.

### Expected

`terraform destroy` removes the diagnostic settings it created.

<!-- avm-triage-regression-fixture -->
